subject: Request: current security assessment for Hosted API + secure transfer options
messages:
From: Max Turner <max.turner@acmepayments.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: current security assessment for Hosted API

Hi Dylan,

Hope you’re well — procurement and security are pushing to close our onboarding checklist this week. Can you share the latest third-party assessment for Redwood’s Hosted API (the most recent penetration test / vuln assessment and the corresponding remediation summary)? Specifically we need: 1) the most recent pen test report PDF, 2) a short remediation matrix that maps findings to fixes/timestamps, and 3) a one-paragraph scope statement that confirms Hosted API is in-scope (we understand Dedicated/Private may be separate).

Given the sensitivity, we need a secure transfer method (presigned link or ShareFile) and a contact who can answer a couple of quick follow-ups on remediation items. Is this possible today?

Thanks,
Max Turner
Senior Security Engineer — Acme Payments
max.turner@acmepayments.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Max Turner <max.turner@acmepayments.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: current security assessment for Hosted API

Hi Max — thanks for the note and the clear checklist. I’m looping in Laura from InfoSec and Priya from our customer success team. Laura — can you confirm we can share the latest assessment and remediation matrix via a presigned URL (or SFTP if you prefer) and include a one-paragraph scope summary that explicitly mentions Hosted API? Priya will coordinate timing with Acme for any follow-ups.

Max — we should be able to get this to you today or tomorrow; Laura will confirm transfer method and expiry window. If you have a preferred transfer mechanism or required retention window for the link, say so and we’ll accommodate.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Max Turner <max.turner@acmepayments.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: current security assessment for Hosted API

Hi Max — thanks for the request. Per Dylan’s note, I’m sharing the artifacts and a short scope/remediation summary below. We’re using a presigned S3 link that expires in 7 days; if you need a shorter window or an IP-restricted transfer, let me know and we’ll re-issue.

Secure files (download within 7 days):
https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-secure-shares/acme-pt-20260803?X-Amz-Expires=604800

Attachments included in the package:
- redwood_pt_report_2024_v3.pdf (full assessment — external vendor engagement, includes executive summary and technical findings)
- remediation_matrix_acme_v1.xlsx (mapping of findings to owners, fix dates, and verification notes)

Scope (one-paragraph):
This assessment covers Redwood’s Hosted API production environment (control plane and inference runtime serving hosted API customers), including external-facing API endpoints, authentication flows, and the cloud-hosted inference fleet. Excluded from scope: Dedicated reserved clusters and Private/VPC on-prem deployments (those are validated under separate engagements).

Remediation summary (high-level):
- Critical: 1 finding (JWT key rotation misconfiguration) — mitigated and verified on 2026-06-12; compensating monitoring added.
- High: 3 findings (rate-limiting gaps, insecure default logging) — remediated between 2026-06-15 and 2026-07-02; verification tests completed.
- Medium/Low: several informational and hardening items — scheduled or implemented as noted in remediation_matrix_acme_v1.xlsx.

Evidence notes: the PDF is vendor-signed; the remediation matrix includes ticket links (internal) and verification dates. We redact internal IPs and customer-specific traces in the shared PDF. If Acme needs an unredacted copy under an NDA, we can arrange an encrypted transfer and separate NDAs for that exchange.

If you want a short attestation letter for procurement (one-paragraph confirming the results and remediation status), I can produce that today. Priya — please propose times for a 15-minute follow-up with Max if he wants to go through the high/critical items.

Attachments: redwood_pt_report_2024_v3.pdf; remediation_matrix_acme_v1.xlsx

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Information Security — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Max Turner <max.turner@acmepayments.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: current security assessment for Hosted API

Hi Laura / Dylan — received the link and downloaded both files successfully. Quick follow-ups: 1) could you provide that one-paragraph attestation for procurement (we need a signed/emailed statement that the critical finding was remediated and verified), and 2) is there a short point of contact for any technical questions on the remediation (someone who can answer verification steps and test evidence)?

If possible, we’d like the attestation by EOD today so procurement can finalize our onboarding checklist. Thanks for the fast turnaround — appreciate the clarity in the scope statement.

Regards,
Max Turner
Senior Security Engineer — Acme Payments
max.turner@acmepayments.com
